zh.sourceText: 某牙膏广告宣称：『80% 的牙医推荐本品牌！』广告的潜台词是：牙医都认可，所以它最专业。可是【gap:g1】，我们凭什么相信这个比例？

textRefs.conclusion_1: 牙医都认可，所以它最专业
textRefs.gap_g1: 这 80% 是从多少牙医里统计的？调查怎么做？受访者是否收过品牌方的好处？

g1: 这 80% 是从多少牙医里统计的？调查怎么做？受访者是否收过品牌方的好处？
这款牙膏的泡沫非常丰富
这款牙膏的包装设计很时尚

hints: 先点出广告的结论（潜台词）
再补上被省略的信息——比例背后的统计细节
「80% 牙医推荐」：统计了多少人？方法是什么？有没有利益关系？
zh.explanation: 「80% 牙医推荐」听起来权威，但省略了三件要命的事：样本量（可能只问了 10 个）、调查方法（线上自选？）、利益关系（受访者是否收钱）。数字本身不会骗人，省略了背景的数字才最会骗人。

en.sourceText: A toothpaste ad claims: "80% of dentists recommend our brand!" The implication is: dentists all approve, so it is the most professional. But 【gap:g1】, why should we trust this percentage?

textRefs.conclusion_1: dentists all approve, so it is the most professional
textRefs.gap_g1: How many dentists was this 80% based on? How was the survey done? Were the respondents paid by the brand?

g1: How many dentists was this 80% based on? How was the survey done? Were the respondents paid by the brand?
This toothpaste produces very rich foam
This toothpaste has a trendy package design

hints: Point out the ad's conclusion (the implication) first
Then patch the omitted information — the statistical details behind the percentage
"80% of dentists": how many were surveyed? what method? any conflicts of interest?
en.explanation: "80% of dentists recommend" sounds authoritative but omits three crucial facts: sample size (maybe only 10 dentists), survey method (self-selected online?), and conflicts of interest (were respondents paid?). Numbers don't lie — numbers with their context stripped away are the ones that lie best.
